title: Get started with tidyusmacro
text: getBLSFiles() downloads processes data Bureau Labor Statistics flat files: CPI, CPI-W, chained CPI, PPI (commodity industry), import/export prices, ECI, ECEC, productivity, JOLTS, CPS, CES, CEX, average prices, state/area employment (SAE), local area unemployment (LAUS). Call blsSources() full, current list sizes descriptions. BLS asks email address user agent flat-file downloads. Every source carries freq ("monthly", "quarterly", "semiannual", "annual") is_average (TRUE BLS-computed rows like M13 annual average S01 half-year average). Observed values dated first month. Computed averages dated last day period cover: M13 2024 2024-12-31, S01 2024-06-30. keeps annual average date real December observation, grouping date across many series silently double-count. Averages share date , use is_average freq need separate , pass include_averages = FALSE drop outright. CPI arrives monthly relative importance already attached, BLS’s cu.aspect file: weight, base observation month’s 1-month change, weight_12mo, base 12-month change – weights 1-month 12-month contribution calculation actually need, already shifted right month (see ?getBLSFiles dating convention; lag either column ). Coverage U.S. city average March 2012 forward; weights NA outside rather back-filled. keyed item code month, series ID, seasonally adjusted series carry . Pass weights = FALSE skip extra download. getCPIAspects() returns rest metadata file: BLS’s contribution decomposition (W1, WC), median standard errors published percent changes (M1, MC), seasonal factors (F). getCESRevisions() downloads revisions table Current Employment Survey (CES) total jobs numbers straight BLS website.
code: cpi_data <- getBLSFiles(data_source = "cpi", email = "user@example.com") jolts_data <- getBLSFiles(data_source = "jolts", email = "user@example.com")  # Newer sources use the same call; blsFiles() lists what's available within one blsFiles("ppi", "user@example.com") ppi_data <- getBLSFiles("ppi", "user@example.com") library(dplyr)  # Contribution of each item to the 12-month change in the all items index, # in percentage points. contributions <- cpi_data |>   filter(area_code == "0000", seasonal == "U", periodicity_code == "R") |>   arrange(series_id, date) |>   group_by(series_id) |>   mutate(contribution_12m = weight_12mo * (value / lag(value, 12) - 1)) |>   ungroup() effects <- getCPIAspects("user@example.com", aspect_type = c("W1", "WC")) revisions_df <- getCESRevisions()

title: Get started with tidyusmacro
text: getNIPAFiles() downloads formats BEA NIPA data flat files, either monthly quarterly values. getPCEInflation() loads processes Personal Consumption Expenditures (PCE) inflation data weights growth measures. getDallasTrimPCE() builds component-level panel underlying Dallas Fed Trimmed Mean PCE inflation rate: monthly price changes, Fisher expenditure-share weights, flags components trimmed month. Useful replicating trimmed-mean rate analyzing gets trimmed.
code: nipa_quarterly <- getNIPAFiles(type = "Q") nipa_monthly <- getNIPAFiles(type = "M") pce_monthly <- getPCEInflation("M") pce_quarterly <- getPCEInflation("Q") # Default 24/31 Dallas Fed trim panel <- getDallasTrimPCE()  # Replicate the monthly trimmed-mean rate panel |>   dplyr::filter(!is_trimmed) |>   dplyr::group_by(date) |>   dplyr::summarize(trim_pce = weighted.mean(price_change, weight))

text: logLinearProjection() performs log-linear projections historical data. Designed use within dplyr verbs.
code: library(dplyr)  # Stands in for a real series; in practice this comes from getFRED() or # getNIPAFiles(). Real GDP, billions of chained 2017 dollars, SAAR. gdp_data <- data.frame(   date = seq(as.Date("2015-01-01"), by = "quarter", length.out = 40),   gdp  = 18000 * 1.005^(0:39) )  # Fit the trend on 2015-2019 and project it through the end of the series. gdp_data %>%   mutate(projection = logLinearProjection(     date = date,     value = gdp,     start_date = "2015-01-01",     end_date = "2019-12-01"   ))

what: Downloading and Cleaning U.S. Macroeconomic Data
title: Downloading and Cleaning U.S. Macroeconomic Data
text: Utilities retrieve tidy U.S. macroeconomic data series public government data providers. Functions streamline access series Bureau Labor Statistics (BLS) full data flat files popular releases like employment inflation, Bureau Economic Analysis National Income Product Accounts (NIPA) tables give GDP related accounts, Federal Reserve Bank St. Louis Federal Reserve Economic Data (FRED). return consistent, tidy data frames ready modeling graphics. tools pull entire flat files corresponding set, makes useful exploring data, -depth research, also real-time analysis following releases. BLS BEA pulls updated right go live. (FRED usually updated 40 minutes later.) Though note jobs numbers can take 5-10 minutes right launch time; API calls might work better. package also includes helpers date alignment, log-linear projections, common macro diagnostics, along convenience plot builders quick publication-quality charts R tidyverse’s ggplot2 format.

what: Download and Process Bureau of Labor Statistics Data — getBLSFiles
title: Download and Process Bureau of Labor Statistics Data — getBLSFiles
text: Downloads processes data Bureau Labor Statistics (BLS) flat files. Supports multiple data sources including CPI, ECI, JOLTS, CPS, CES, others. function retrieves main data file along associated metadata files, merges , returns tidy tibble ready analysis.

title: Download and Process Bureau of Labor Statistics Data — getBLSFiles
code: getBLSFiles(   data_source,   email,   weights = TRUE,   include_averages = TRUE,   file = NULL,   max_mb = 500 )

title: Download and Process Bureau of Labor Statistics Data — getBLSFiles
text: data_source Character string specifying BLS data source. Call blsSources() full, current list sizes descriptions. Commonly used values: "cpi" Consumer Price Index - current data "cpi_w" CPI, urban wage earners; basis Social Security COLA "cpi_chained" Chained CPI (C-CPI-U); basis tax bracket indexing "eci" Employment Cost Index (quarterly) "ecec" Employer Costs Employee Compensation (quarterly) "cex" Consumer Expenditure Survey "jolts" Job Openings Labor Turnover Survey "cps" Current Population Survey "ces" Current Employment Statistics - series "ces_allemp" Current Employment Statistics - employees, seasonally adjusted "ces_total" Current Employment Statistics - total nonfarm employment "averageprice" Average price data - current "food" Average price data - food items "ppi" Producer Price Index, commodity "ppi_industry" Producer Price Index, industry product "import_export" Import export price indexes "productivity" Major sector productivity unit labor costs "laus" Local Area Unemployment Statistics ("su") "sae" State Area Employment, Hours, Earnings ("se") "se" "su" still work deprecated: "su" real BLS prefix (chained CPI), old alias squatting , reused chained CPI added. warn redirect "sae"/"laus". email Character string email address. Required BLS identifying API users. Set HTTP User-Agent header. weights Logical; data_source = "cpi" . TRUE (default), also downloads cu.aspect attaches monthly relative importance plus BLS's published contributions. Ignored every data source. Set FALSE skip extra ~31 MB download. include_averages Logical, default TRUE. BLS period codes include just monthly/quarterly observations computed averages: M13 (annual average), S01/S02 (half-year average), S03 (annual average), Q05 (annual average). flagged via is_average column rather dropped, sources (CEX publishes A01) rows exist. Set FALSE drop , e.g. group_by(date) across many series average row otherwise land December date year's real December observation. file Character, optional. Picks non-default data file within survey, e.g. file = "data.21.Aggregates" PPI's FD-ID aggregates. Call blsFiles(data_source, email) see exists. Required discontinued (tier 4) surveys, default file. max_mb Numeric, default 500. Refuse download data file larger without explicit override (e.g. osh_characteristics 2.9 GB). Set Inf disable.

Additional metadata columns vary data source (e.g., item codes, industry codes, area codes) CPI weights = TRUE, four columns: weight Relative importance, percent items, base month 1-month change ending observation month. weight 1-month contribution; lag . See dating note . weight_12mo Relative importance base month 12-month change ending observation month; weight 12-month contribution effect_1m BLS's published effect 1-month items change, percentage points. Seasonally adjusted rows . effect_12m BLS's published effect 12-month items change, percentage points. seasonally adjusted rows .

title: Download and Process Bureau of Labor Statistics Data — getBLSFiles
text: Relative importance comes cu.aspect (aspect type ""), BLS restamps every CPI release. Three things join worth knowing: keyed area_code + item_code + date, series_id. BLS publishes relative importance seasonally adjusted series (CUUR...), weight describes item, adjustment, joining series_id return NA seasonally adjusted work. Codes rather names, BLS renames items codes stable. Coverage U.S. city average (area_code == "0000") March 2012 forward. Outside window weight NA rather back-filled: imputed weight looks like real one worse missing value. See BLS relative importance archive pre-2012 backfill. row cu.aspect stamped month t carries relative importance BLS labels month t-1. one thing file reliably produces --one errors, worth stating twice: weight want change ending month t row dated t, lag . Verified June 2026 release, "Relative importance May 2026" column Tables 6 7 matches 2026-06-01 rows 307 items exactly 2026-05-01 rows 43. shift BLS's published "Relative importance, December YYYY" table January YYYY+1 row. Accordingly weight row dated t needs lag, weight_12mo row dated t-11 – eleven months back, RI labeled t-12 lives t-11 row. weight columns joined month index, never row position. BLS omits rows entirely intermittently priced items rather writing NA, positional lag borrows wrong month's weight without warning.

title: Build the Dallas Fed trimmed-mean PCE component panel — getDallasTrimPCE
text: Weights Fisher-style: unweighted average expenditure share evaluated base prices P[t-1] quantities Q[t-1] Q[t], renormalized sum 1 within month. Real quantity computed nominal / price BEA NIPA Tables 2.4.5U 2.4.4U respectively (equivalent Table 2.4.6U per Dallas Fed's MATLAB note, available across full sample without chained-dollar gaps). Trim assignment simple rank-based version: components sorted within month price_change, cumulative weight accumulated, components whose running cumulative weight alpha flagged "lower", components whose cumulative weight adding contribution 1 - beta flagged "upper". Boundary components straddle either threshold kept (treated interior). Dallas Fed's exact fractional-boundary handling enters rate calculation , panel-builder; resulting headline rate matches Dallas Fed series within basis points. Months without full cross-sectional coverage (.e., component missing month last) weight, is_trimmed, trim_side set NA.

title: tidyusmacro 0.2.0
text: getDallasTrimPCE() downloads component-level data underlying Dallas Fed Trimmed Mean PCE inflation rate returns tidy panel trimming weights trim-side flags. getUnrateFRED() retrieves unemployment labor force levels FRED computes unemployment rate. date_breaks_gg() date_breaks_n() provide evenly spaced date breaks ggplot2 axes. getBLSFiles() supports Consumer Expenditure Survey flat files (data_source = "cex"). New dataset dallasTrimPCEcomponents maps PCE line items Dallas Fed trimmed-mean components.

title: tidyusmacro 0.2.0
text: getFRED() downloads via httr::GET() explicit user agent, fixing intermittent “HTTP/2 stream closed cleanly” failures FRED’s CSV endpoint. getBLSFiles() longer produces duplicate .x/.y columns lookup files share metadata column names; shared metadata columns prefixed lookup file name. getBLSFiles() now restores user’s HTTPUserAgent option exit. logLinearProjection() longer calls deprecated dplyr::cur_data_all(), warned every use dplyr >= 1.1.0; now uses dplyr::pick(). Calls using old pre-0.2.0 string interface fail informative error pointing new interface. Added testthat suite covering logLinearProjection().
